extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, researchers, agency staff, and commenters who use FederalRegister.gov to find, read, cite, draft, or comment on Federal Register documents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using FederalRegister.gov: how to find and cite documents, understand the site's legal status and public inspection list, submit formal comments, use developer resources, and follow drafting and accessibility resources when preparing Federal Register documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status / unofficial prototype
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a “Web 2.0” version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register, and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO’s govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documents posted are XML renditions and each document includes a link to the corresponding official PDF on govinfo.gov. Until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register (ACFR) issues a regulation granting it official legal status, the XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts. Those relying on it for legal research should verify against the official edition on govinfo.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Public Inspection page
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Inspection web page on FederalRegister.gov offers a preview of documents scheduled to appear in the next day’s Federal Register issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Public Inspection page may also include documents scheduled for later issues, at the request of the issuing agency. Use the Public Inspection list for previews but confirm final publication in the official edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission channels — site feedback vs formal comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Site Feedback' tool and Federal Register email addresses are only intended for users to submit technical questions and comments on the functionality of the FederalRegister.gov website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools cannot be used to submit comments on rulemaking actions or to petition agencies on public policy issues; the Office of the Federal Register has no authority or ability to process rulemaking comments submitted via Site Feedback. To submit formal comments on rulemakings, use Regulations.gov or the site’s 'Submit a Formal Comment' feature which connects to the official docket system.

rubrics_metrics.name: New 'Submit a Formal Comment' feature
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov added the ability to comment on a document without leaving the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This feature works in cooperation with Regulations.gov and allows users to submit formal comments for rulemaking dockets while staying on FederalRegister.gov. Previously users had to leave the site to submit comments on Regulations.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Features — active/agency-included links
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency has included links as part of the document text, FederalRegister.gov activates those links using the text in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links may not work if the original published document contained an error or if the target website is no longer at that location. The site also provides automated legal links (where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Features — sidebar and utility bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The document utility bar runs along the left side of the document and scrolls with you down the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the utility bar icons to access the Public Inspection version and the official electronic format of the published document (PDF on govinfo.gov), to print using the printer icon, and to share (email, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search tools and citation searchability
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov offers a basic search box and an advanced search. The 'Search' pull-down shows various search options including Document Search, Advanced Document Search, and Public Inspection Search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can search by full text or by citation (for example: '75 FR 12345' or '75 Fed. Reg. 12345'). The site provides tips and examples for using complex search terms and how to combine search options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking to and citing FederalRegister.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register documents can be linked and cited in a variety of ways, and the site explains various linking patterns and citation formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the site's explained patterns when referencing documents; use links to the official PDF on govinfo.gov for legal citations and verify citation formats provided in the guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document drafting & research resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The site lists drafting and research links to help understand the document drafting process and research Federal Register documents, such as the Document Drafting Handbook, Incorporation by Reference (IBR) Handbook, Federal Register Bulletins, Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010, PlainLanguage.gov, Thesaurus of Indexing Terms, and GPO Page Rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these resources when preparing Federal Register submissions to ensure correct drafting, proper incorporation by reference, and plain-language compliance. They are intended to improve the quality and accessibility of submitted documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility standards for documents and site
rubrics_metrics.description: The site is designed following Section 508 and W3C accessibility design guidelines and uses text-based files and PDF files which are text-accessible through Adobe PDF tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and submitters should ensure PDFs are text-accessible and that content meets accessibility standards. The site provides information on assistance for visually impaired users and other accessibility resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developer resources, data provenance, and APIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register data originates with the files used to produce print and PDF editions; these are transformed into bulk XML files and MODS metadata files by GPO and exposed via REST API and developer documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers may use the REST API, the maintained Ruby API client (gem), and other clients; source code for FederalRegister.gov is open source and available on GitHub. Use the provided API docs and clients to access and integrate Federal Register data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register Workshop as user training
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register Workshop is a roughly three-hour presentation by an Office of the Federal Register staff member describing the Federal Register system and how to use it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The workshop explains the relationship between the Federal Register and the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) and provides practical instruction for users and agency customers; attending is recommended for deeper understanding of the publication system.
